title: Rehearse natural-language alignment through a host Adapter

requirement.summary: Add a vendor-neutral reference Adapter journey in which a user speaks naturally, a host-owned semantic materializer creates strict ephemeral alignment records, AgentGov asks exactly one useful question at a time, and the host records the final single-select without requiring user-authored JSON or internal commands.

objective.rationale: The strict Core transport is not yet the promised low-friction user experience. A small end-to-end host-side slice must prove that ordinary conversation can drive the protocol without moving raw chat into Core or making the user author governance records.

goal: Add a foreground reference Alignment Adapter API with a replaceable host semantic materializer, natural-language request and answer methods, host-owned final selection recording, a privacy-safe journey trace, and explicit interaction-burden metrics, then exercise the complete flow against the existing in-memory Core session.
non_goals: Do not implement semantic inference inside AgentGov Core or claim deterministic understanding of arbitrary natural-language intent.
Do not bundle or call a model, retain raw request or answer text, store transcripts, or persist dialogue across process restarts.
Do not add a vendor-specific Adapter, daemon, dashboard, production UI, authenticated callback, or external integration.
Do not require the human to author JSON, contract IDs, digests, timestamps, actor fields, or internal CLI commands.
Do not automatically change requirements, architecture, tasks, sessions, code scope, Git, deployment, publication, or release state.
Do not change stable 0.2.1, immutable v0.3.0rc1, release metadata, workflows, consumer repositories, or external systems.
acceptance_signals: A vendor-neutral host materializer boundary accepts raw natural-language request or answer text and returns only an existing strict normalized alignment-context or clarification-update record; Core never receives the raw text.

The reference Adapter starts from one natural-language request, returns the exact one-question Core prompt, accepts a natural-language answer, and returns either the next one-question prompt or the existing stable final single-select.
The host records a selected option through the existing human-decision result contract without asking the user to construct JSON, IDs, digests, timestamps, actor metadata, or internal commands.

A privacy-safe journey result exposes normalized Core responses and interaction-burden metrics while retaining no raw request, raw answer, transcript, source content, credential, model identity, or absolute host path.
Invalid materializer output, stale state, premature answer or decision, non-offered option, and raw-content declarations fail before the Adapter advances its Core session or journey metrics.

A complete independent test rehearsal proves one natural request, one natural clarification answer, one single-select decision, zero user-authored structured records, one governance decision episode, and no repository or external mutation.
Existing alignment and lifecycle transport behavior remains compatible, and focused/full tests, current-task, scope, repository, schema, compile, and diff validation pass.
validation_commands: python -m unittest tests.test_reference_alignment_adapter tests.test_alignment_transport tests.test_clarification_dialogue tests.test_human_decision tests.test_task_contract -v

items: A host semantic materializer can still misunderstand or bias the user's center, drift, normalized answer, candidate choices, or recommendation even when Core validates structure correctly.
An Adapter could accidentally retain or forward raw conversation while presenting the journey as privacy-safe.
A scripted test could be mistaken for production semantic inference unless the replaceable materializer and current capability boundary are explicit.
Friction metrics could encourage premature decisions unless clarification answers remain separate from governance decision episodes.

stop_conditions: Stop if the flow requires Core to receive or retain raw natural language, transcript, source content, credential, model identity, or absolute host path.
Stop if arbitrary semantic inference would have to be falsely represented as deterministic AgentGov behavior.
Stop if the Coding Agent or Adapter can select the final human direction or impersonate a human clarification answer.
Stop if invalid materializer output partially advances Core state or interaction metrics.
Stop if the journey mutates project, task, architecture, session, scope, code, Git, deployment, publication, release, or external state.
Stop before any Git write, Hook installation, release, consumer mutation, deployment, or external-system write.

decision.rationale: The user reviewed the delivered natural-language Adapter rehearsal and explicitly approved documenting the next semantic-review compute and risk-routing architecture on 2026-08-06. This task is paused for routing hygiene only; it does not claim merge, publication, or release.
